title: Classes and this
summary: Bundle data with the functions that use it, keep fields private, and know what this (or self) points to.

sections.heading: A class is a blueprint
body: A class describes what each object will hold and what it can do. The constructor (`__init__` in Python) sets up a new object; methods are functions that work on it.
Inside, `this` (JavaScript) or `self` (Python) means "the object this method was called on".

sections.heading: Private fields and getters
body: Fields starting with `#` in JavaScript cannot be touched from outside the class. Python has no true private fields; a leading underscore means "please do not use this from outside".
A getter (`get total()`, or `@property` in Python) is read like a field but runs code.

sections.heading: this depends on how you call it
body: In JavaScript, `this` is decided at the moment of the call: `obj.method()` sets `this` to `obj`. Take the method out on its own and call it, and `this` is `undefined`.
Arrow functions do not have their own `this`; they keep the one from where they were written. That is why arrow functions are safe to pass around as callbacks.

hi Ada
this is undefined
hi Ada

mistakes: Forgetting `new` when creating an object in JavaScript.
Forgetting `self` as the first parameter of a Python method, or forgetting `self.` when using a field.
Passing `obj.method` as a callback and losing `this`. Use an arrow function: `() => obj.method()`.
